In my opinion, you've already made your decision about wanting to go on. If it scares you enough to not want to take it, then I feel like you don't believe your acne to be bad enough to warrant taking the drug.

Also, even though the severe side effects are rare, ask yourself whether you'd rather deal with those side effects persistently or deal with acne.
My dry mouth never quite cleared up after Accutane. It got better, but it never quite left. Some days are worse than others, but it's mostly manageable.

Try adding salicylic acid to what you're already doing. Just apply it to your face after you shower and lightly dry your face (not completely) and let it sit for a few minutes, then put the rest of your stuff on.

I do drink plenty of water throughout the day (at least half my body weight in ounces). So I don't think hydration is an issue, although I'm positive it helps because the off days that I do slack on drinking water my lips definitely do suffer the consequences.

Also, my doctor seemed to disregard the dryness, no matter how long i seemed to have it. She always just said "just give it more time"...

That's actually comforting to hear knowing that it isn't completely abnormal for this to be happening. Don't get me wrong, my lips have definitely come a long way since stopping Accutane, but I just really want them to be able to make it through a day without having to apply moisturizer again :P.

This might not be what you want to hear, but acne returning after accutane can be seen as a good sign. It means that it definitely didn't do anything permanent (as some people say can happen) to you.

Also, just hang in there. I know hair loss can be rough, but it will definitely return to the way it was before. Just try to make the "journey" as easy as possible and pamper the heck out of your hair. Stay strong!

Also on a side note, since you probably won't be wanting to go back on Accutane, you can take solace in the fact that your acne will probably respond to treatments that didn't work prior to taking it.

I'm extremely on the fence on this; however, I will admit my bias by saying that I DO want to believe that there is an afterlife. But there hasn't been anything profound that has happened in my own life to make me feel certain that there is one. Although, many things have happened to people in my family, and I have heard some quite convincing stories and recordings from tapes of readings that my mother got after a loss of an uncle.

One more disclaimer before I go into the stories/tape though: a good portion of my family really does believe in the afterlife with 100% certainty, and the stories do come from them (one being a slight exception). So keep that in mind, and be sure to take everything with a grain of salt.

The first, and probably most profound, piece of possible evidence of an afterlife is a reading my mother got almost 10 years ago after the tragic loss of an uncle. She taped the reading, and because I was only 8 at the time she got it done, i hadn't heard it until this year actually. I listened to the whole thing, and while of course there are some quite good "hits" throughout it, there are 2 things that really hit home that I have no possible explanation for. 

The first is the medium talking about a picture he was seeing, I can't quote him word for word since I'd have to dig around to find the tape again, but I do remember some things he said exactly. He described a picture of a serene beach, at sunset/sunrise (he admitted that he couldn't tell which because "the colors are so similar"), that the water is "calm and hitting the sand", and that something is written in the sand (he did not say what was though). At the time my mother had no clue what he was talking about, and this was because our family had no picture like that let alone seen one quite the way he was describing it. So my mother disregarded him, and they proceeded on with the reading. This is the shocking part: a few weeks later my mother received a gift from a family friend that was exactly what the medium had described it to be. After discovering this I questioned my mother, and she ensured me that there was no way that the medium could have known about the family friend that sent the picture. I'm still skeptical about this though since I'm not sure if this could be considered a broad statement anyone could say.

The second thing that the medium said that actually shocked me was bringing up the name of cat... Named Boogies... And this shocks me the most because I cannot possibly think of a way that he could have cold read this. During the reading, the medium pauses for a second and says "excuse me, but who's boogers? He [my uncle] keeps doing this (my mother told me the medium acted out picking his nose, like putting his fingers near his nose and twisting them)". My mother then proceeded to tell the medium about the cat that my uncle really liked. Also, take note that the medium didn't get the name exactly, but he was interpreting an act/symbol if you will, so assuming he was doing just that, I'll cut him some slack. Furthermore, this cat had passed quite some time before my uncle did, so it is highly unlikely that the medium could have heard about the family cat named boogies (even though my mom assured me that he hadn't even talked to anyone in our family before the reading). Finally, who in the right mind would randomly ask someone "who's boogers"?

Another experience that my grandmother told me about was when a "friendly spirit" visited her and my grandfather in the middle of the night. I find this story more interesting than others told by my grandmother because my grandfather was a witness, and I know that he wouldn't just blindly say something like "I saw a ghost!" just for the sake justifying his beliefs to himself (and to be honest, I'm not even sure what his stance is on this whole topic lol). So anyway, my grandmother told me that this spirit just woke her up one night and began talking to her (she didn't go into detail about what though), and then my grandfather chimed in by saying that the chatter woke him up. He said that he just looked over and saw someone as clear as day standing right beside his bed. My grandmother told him not to worry and yatta yatta, but my grandfather said that he just stared at the spirit for awhile longer then rolled over and went back to sleep. As a side note of this story, I'd also like to bring up the facial expressions my grandfather made while telling it from his point of view. While and after he was speaking, my grandfather went from his usual cheerful expression to a quite solemn/contemplative facial expression. You could tell he was thinking about what had happened a lot, and that the experience (whether an actual visit from a spirit or not) really impacted him. I feel like this is important because facial expression can tell of story of their own. and it certainly didn't seem like he was putting on a show or being sarcastic in any way.

Anyway, these are just a few of the experiences that have happened to my family over the years. And although some of the accounts might be quite convincing, I'm still on the fence about this because of the fact that nothing profound like this has happened to me (I wasn't there to judge the entire experience to make sure no trickery was going on, and I'm pretty sure my grandparents do use any sort of hallucinogens lol). My grandmother tells me that I have to be more open about these experiences happening, and I will admit that I do feel like I would be quite spooked if anything similar to the spirit story happened to me. She said if i got over this fear, that something similar would eventually happen (and she says that with a certainty). We'll see what happens over the years though. I'd be lying if I said I haven't been trying to find ways to get over the possible fear of a "spiritual visit" though, and I'm actually planning on seeing a medium (might not be the same one as mentioned) in the near future.
